## Citation

Robey-Bond, S.M., Barrantes-Reynolds, R., Bond, J.P., Wallace, S.S., & Bandaru, V. (2008). Clostridium Acetobutylicum 8-Oxoguanine DNA Glycosylase (Ogg) Differs from Eukaryotic Oggs with Respect to Opposite Base Discrimination. *Biochemistry*, 47(29), 7626-7636.

## Abstract

8-Oxoguanine is a common DNA lesion caused by oxidative damage. Ogg enzymes catalyze the removal of 8-oxoguanine paired with cytosine. This study characterizes the bacterial Ogg from *Clostridium acetobutylicum* and reveals important functional differences compared to eukaryotic enzymes.

## Key Findings

- *Clostridium* Ogg shows opposite base discrimination compared to eukaryotic enzymes
- Bacterial enzyme preferentially excises 8-oxoguanine:adenine pairs
- Eukaryotic enzymes preferentially remove 8-oxoguanine:cytosine pairs
- Structural basis for substrate specificity differences
- Evolutionary significance of base discrimination strategies

## Methods

- Enzyme kinetics and substrate specificity assays
- DNA substrate synthesis and characterization
- Biochemical analysis of lesion recognition
- Structural comparisons with eukaryotic homologs

## Role

As a co-author, I contributed to bioinformatics analysis and evolutionary comparisons of Ogg proteins.
